subject: computer-science
title: Graphs: Representations and Traversal
welcome_lead: Vertices, edges and ways to walk them.
meta_desc: A-Level CS: directed vs undirected, weighted graphs, BFS and DFS.
final_note: Once you can traverse, you can solve almost anything on a graph.

concepts.def: A graph whose edges have a direction.
A graph whose edges carry a numeric weight.
A V x V table where entry [i][j] indicates an edge.
Per vertex, a list of its neighbours — compact for sparse graphs.

walkthroughs.body_html: In a directed graph edges have direction (a one-way street). In a weighted graph each edge carries a number — distance, cost or time. Many real networks combine both.
An adjacency matrix takes O(V^2) space — fast for dense graphs. An adjacency list takes O(V+E) — better when the graph is sparse, which is the usual case.
BFS uses a queue, exploring layer by layer — finds shortest path on unweighted graphs. DFS uses a stack (or recursion) and dives deep — useful for cycles and topological sort.
